contract: applyPatch(source, patch, options?) accepts a unified diff string, the single-file array returned by parsePatch, or a single record from that array; parsePatch always returns an array of file records. Multi-file arrays or strings should be passed to applyPatches; applyPatch throws an Error for multi-file input. Returns false when the context does not match. If the existing source has no trailing newline and no explicit EOF marker, ordinary appends or replacements preserve the lack of a trailing newline; if the existing source has a trailing newline, it is preserved. A newline at the end of the patch text is not itself the target file's EOF state. When creating a file from an empty source, if the added lines have no missing-newline marker, the lines are newline-separated and the file has a trailing newline. \ No newline at end of file immediately following a deleted line indicates no trailing newline on the old side; immediately following an added line, it indicates no trailing newline on the new side; an old-side marker appearing on its own can add a trailing newline, while a new-side marker can remove a trailing newline. Deleting all content returns an empty string and does not generate a phantom newline. applyPatches uses the same byte-level rules for each file and serially invokes loadFile(record, callback(error, source)) and patched(record, result, acknowledgement(error)), in that order; it processes the next file only after the acknowledgement callback, then finally complete(error?); on success, error is null or undefined, and on failure, the error is passed through. Topics still awaiting disclosure of the relevant follow-up questions remain pending; that does not mean the requirement does not exist.
